desc:
You play a game on the integer array nums. In one move you choose any element with value x and remove it, earning x points. Right after that move, every element equal to x - 1 and every element equal to x + 1 is also removed from the array (you earn nothing for those).

You may make as many moves as you like, in any order, until you stop or the array is empty. Return the maximum total number of points you can earn.
hints: If you take one copy of x, you may as well take every copy of x: the extra copies are never in conflict with anything new.
Group the elements by value. Taking value v is worth v × count(v) and forbids taking v-1 and v+1.
That is House Robber over the values 1..10,000: best(v) = max(best(v-1), best(v-2) + v × count(v)).
editorial: Once you take a value x, the neighbours x-1 and x+1 vanish but other copies of x do not, so taking all copies of x is always at least as good. Therefore the game is really a choice of values: the set of values you pick must not contain two consecutive integers, and picking value v yields v * count(v) points.

Build an array gain[v] = v * count(v) for v up to the maximum value, then run the House Robber recurrence best(v) = max(best(v-1), best(v-2) + gain[v]) with two rolling variables. Time O(n + max value), space O(max value).
